questions.question: You are writing a Python application that extracts fields from receipts by using Azure Content Understanding. Which client class should you create?

options.why: Correct. ContentUnderstandingClient from azure-ai-contentunderstanding runs analyzers.
TextAnalyticsClient is used for Azure Language text analysis.
SpeechRecognizer is part of the Speech SDK for speech to text.
ImageAnalysisClient is used for Azure Vision image analysis.

questions.explanation: The azure-ai-contentunderstanding package provides ContentUnderstandingClient for running Content Understanding analyzers.

questions.question: Your code calls client.begin_analyze(analyzer_id="prebuilt-invoice", inputs=[...]). What must the code do next to obtain the extracted fields?

options.text: Call result() on the returned poller
options.why: Correct. begin_analyze returns a poller, and result() waits for the long-running operation to complete.

options.text: Read the fields property of the poller directly
options.why: The poller represents the operation; the fields are available only in the completed result.

options.text: Call images.generate with the same input
options.why: images.generate creates images and is unrelated to analysis.
Conversations are used for multi-turn model and agent interactions.

questions.explanation: Analysis is a long-running operation. The poller returned by begin_analyze provides the analysis result through result().

questions.question: Which TWO properties of an extracted field should an application read to save a value and decide whether it requires human review?

options.why: Correct. value contains the extracted data.
Correct. confidence indicates how certain the service is and can be compared with a threshold.
temperature is a generation parameter for models, not a field property.
b64_json contains image data returned by image generation.

questions.explanation: Each field provides its value and a confidence score. Applications commonly route values below a chosen confidence threshold to a reviewer.

questions.scenario: An application currently extracts invoice fields by calling begin_analyze with the prebuilt-invoice analyzer. The company now wants the same application to summarize recorded support calls.
questions.question: What is the minimum change required?

options.text: Change the analyzer ID to prebuilt-audioSearch and supply the call recording as input
options.why: Correct. The client and analysis flow stay the same; only the analyzer and input change.

options.text: Rewrite the application by using the Speech SDK
options.why: Content Understanding already transcribes and summarizes recorded audio.
Image generation is not needed to summarize calls.

options.text: Change the field method of InvoiceTotal to generate
options.why: Changing an invoice field does not enable audio analysis.

questions.explanation: Content Understanding uses the same client and begin_analyze pattern for every content type. Selecting an audio analyzer and providing the recording is sufficient.

questions.question: A developer wants the ContentUnderstandingClient to authenticate without storing a resource key in code or configuration. What should the developer use?

options.why: Correct. DefaultAzureCredential authenticates with Microsoft Entra ID, so no key is stored.
This stores a key in code, which the requirement prohibits.
Content filters screen harmful content and do not authenticate clients.
Model deployments do not provide client authentication.

questions.explanation: ContentUnderstandingClient accepts a Microsoft Entra ID token credential such as DefaultAzureCredential as an alternative to a key.
